findings.evidence: "Quoting rule: never paste JSON text into a command. Passing \"$NAME\" or \"$(cat file)\" as an argv is safe: a double-quoted expansion is never re-parsed"
findings.fix: Keep the one-line rule (never paste JSON into a command; load it with $(cat ...)). Move the explanation of shell re-parsing to references/design-notes.md, which already holds the reasoning for the rules, and record the move.

findings.evidence: "Step 4: Task review, fix loop, final review — unaffected ... run unmodified on $REPORT_FILE"
findings.fix: Shorten Step 4 to one sentence that names the scope boundary: this skill never touches review, adjudication or the ledger. Do not restate subagent-driven-development's own steps, and record the shortening.

findings.evidence: No previous-version digest was supplied, so the removal check was not run
findings.fix: Run the next judge round with a digest from scripts/audit/audit.py judge-prompt, so the judge can check removed content.

findings.evidence: "Run the block below only at a new round: a restored $FIX_ROUND already counts the round, so the resume path never runs it: at a restored round of 4 or more with no pinned injection_json it goes to ..."
findings.fix: Replace the nested fix-round prose (lines 207-221) with a small decision table keyed on new round vs resume, pinned vs unpinned and round 1-3 vs 4-5. Give each row its action and its reference, so the Process pattern's checkpoints are explicit.

findings.evidence: Steps 0-5 have no progress checklist, even though the workflow spans several mandatory reference reads and blocks run once per plan or once per task
findings.fix: Add a short per-plan and per-task checklist after the NEVER list: config check, start step, task paths, wake arm, Step 2, Step 3, code review, fold, wake close. This keeps the Process pattern trackable.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list holds strong, reasoned items, but host and environment facts that defy assumptions sit inside paragraphs instead of a Gotchas section: every Bash call starts a fresh shell (line 80), Codex workspace-write is not an unconditional boundary (line 268), and an older Node crash is never a reason to switch pairs (line 272)
findings.fix: Add a short ## Gotchas section after NEVER. It lists the fresh-shell scalar loss, the conditional Codex sandbox, the dirname-gives-'.' placeholder trap and the Node crash classed as real_error, each in one line with its consequence. Point the step paragraphs back to it.

findings.evidence: The description opens with implementation mechanics ("resolving a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair for each task's implementer dispatch (native or external CLI)") before user intent, and lacks casual-intent phrasing
findings.fix: Use when running or executing a superpowers implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) under superpowers:subagent-driven-development, even when the user only says 'run my plan task by task with subagents'. Picks a live-quota-checked runtime and model for each task's implementer (native subagent or external CLI such as codex), waits out quotas, escalates stuck fix rounds, starts the plan's unit branch before the first task, and folds, pushes and readies it through ai-kit-commit-fold after the final review. Also chained from ai-kit-spec-execute when it detects such a plan. Not for superpowers:executing-plans (inline, no dispatch point), writing or reviewing a plan, configuring lanes (ai-kit-spec-config), or folding a branch on its own (ai-kit-commit-fold).

findings.evidence: "`references/quota-wake.md` in full before scheduling or printing a wake": SKILL.md never names quota-wake.md, so it is reached only through a second-level reference chain
findings.fix: Name references/quota-wake.md in SKILL.md Step 3 with its trigger: read it only on a quota_cycle or quota outcome that Schedule-or-stop resolves to a wait. Keep it one level deep from SKILL.md.

findings.evidence: Single paragraphs of 100+ words (lines 152, 209, 239, 247, 287) inline the gating, exceptions and commands together, which makes the 296-line body heavy
findings.fix: Keep each step's trigger and its MANDATORY read in SKILL.md. Move the exception detail (the gates and guard recipe, the native audit commands, the Step 5 cleanup commands) into the reference each paragraph already cites: state-management.md#gates-and-guard-inputs, dispatch-external-cli.md#host-config-audit and fold-step.md.

findings.evidence: "On another host, use its own subagent mechanism (or STOP and tell the user to resume by hand)" gives a menu with no default for non-Claude hosts
findings.fix: State the default: use the host's subagent mechanism when the host has one; STOP with the resume instructions only when it has none.

findings.evidence: Several evals carry only 2 assertions (precise-config-active-never-asks, edge-spec-config-missing-stops, precise-host-config-audit-observation), and no eval exercises the Rounds 4-5 escalation with an anchor key or a pinned resume after a quota wait
findings.fix: Add an eval for a resumed task at FIX_ROUND=4 with no pinned injection_json. Assert that the escalation resolve block runs, that ESCALATION_ANCHOR_KEY is not overwritten and that no new round increment happens. Give the 2-assertion evals a third verifiable assertion.

findings.evidence: "Codex sandbox: the workspace-write writable roots and protected paths are defined at https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security." The vendor fact cites its source but no date checked
findings.fix: Append the date the page was checked, for example '(checked YYYY-MM-DD)', or tell the agent to read the behaviour live from `codex --help` or `codex sandbox --help` before relying on it.

findings.evidence: The fix-round branch logic depends on four interacting conditions (new round vs resume, pinned injection, round 1-3 vs 4-5, and session fallback or session-model mode vs ladder). Lines 180, 200-201, 209, 211 and 221 restate them, so walking the restored-round-4-pinned branch takes cross-reading five paragraphs
findings.fix: Add one decision tree in Step 3 that covers every combination and names the action and reference for each leaf: pinned means re-dispatch unchanged; unpinned at 4-5 with session fallback or session-model mode means native on the session model; otherwise the escalation.md resolve block. Then cut the restatements at lines 180, 200-201 and 209 down to pointers to it.

findings.evidence: "Replace `<absolute path to THIS SKILL.md>` with the absolute path of the SKILL.md you just loaded." The fallback for a host that does not expose the loaded path is left to the candidate list without saying so
findings.fix: Add one line: when the host does not expose the SKILL.md path, leave the placeholder as is. The case guard skips it and the remaining candidates resolve the shim.
